studentEmulator.title: Try it yourself — a practice copy of Edura
studentEmulator.missHint: Not that one — look for the control with the purple outline and press it.
studentEmulator.finishedBody: You can now read your board, subscribe to a teacher, top up your wallet and pay from it, and get your ID card. Your real account works exactly the same way.
studentEmulator.sandboxNote: Everything above is practice — the data is invented, no real money moves, and nothing is saved to your account.

screens.receiptsBody: Every payment you make produces a numbered receipt you can download here.
screens.cardHint: Your card is not loaded automatically — press to show it.
screens.coverBody: Your Chemistry subscription is running — {days} days left. You get a notice here when it is about to end.

welcome.title: Welcome — this is a practice copy of Edura
welcome.body: The screen below is Edura exactly as it is, filled with the life of an invented student called Nour. Look around and press whatever you like — nothing here touches your account.

upNext.title: The first thing you see: your next class
upNext.body: At the very top, "Up next" — the subject and the time. That is the question you open the app to answer: where am I meant to be?

record.title: And underneath, your record
record.body: Your attendance rate and your average grade. Both are worked out for you from the attendance actually recorded and the grades your teacher entered.

goSubjects.title: Let's subscribe to a teacher
goSubjects.body: Press "Subjects" in the menu on the side.

openSubject.title: Open a subject
openSubject.body: These are the subjects the platform assigned from your grade and track. Press "Chemistry" to see the groups available.

readGroup.title: Read the group before you join it
readGroup.body: Each group tells you the teacher, the times, the centre and how many students. Check them — those times become your schedule.

fullGroup.title: And this one is full
fullGroup.body: 25 of 25 — no places left, so there is no subscribe button. When that happens you pick another group for the same subject.

subscribe.title: Subscribe to the first group
subscribe.body: Press "Subscribe monthly". The price is on the button before you press it, so you know what you are paying.

subscribed.title: You're subscribed
subscribed.body: The group now says "Subscribed", its lessons appeared in your schedule, and the money came out of your wallet. Let's go and look at that.

balance.title: This is your balance
balance.body: It is worked out from the record below it — every piastre has a line you can look at, rather than a figure written on top.

topUp.title: Top it up
topUp.body: Press "Top up". For real it asks you the amount and takes you to pay by card; here we will add 200 EGP straight away.

afterTopUp.title: Look at the record
afterTopUp.body: The balance went up and a new line appeared. Notice the subscription you paid a moment ago is still there — the record is never erased.

receipt.title: And every payment has a receipt
receipt.body: The receipt is your proof that you paid. If anything goes wrong with the centre, its number is the first thing they will ask you for.

readCode.title: This code is who you are at the centre
readCode.body: Eight characters. Counter staff find you with it in a second instead of spelling your name out. Memorise it or photograph it.

counter.title: How you use it
counter.body: You arrive at the centre, hand over the card or say the code, and staff check you in. Some teachers also ask for a second check-in at the hall door — without it your attendance is not counted.

invite.title: First time here? Practise first
invite.body: A practice copy of Edura with invented data that walks you through it step by step: subscribe to a teacher, top up your wallet, get your card — without spending anything or touching your account.

studentTour.title: A quick tour of Edura

welcome.title: Welcome to Edura 👋
welcome.body: Your account is ready. This tour shows you the things you'll actually do — and it won't just say “this is your wallet”, it will show you how, step by step. You can skip it at any point.

upNext.title: Your next class
upNext.body: The first thing on the page is your next session: the subject, the day and time, the hall, and the teacher.

how.2: At the top you'll find “Up next”
how.3: If it says “no upcoming classes”, you haven't subscribed to a teacher yet

schedule.title: How to see a particular day
schedule.body: The schedule shows your classes by day, and the details of each one when you tap it.

how.2: Pick the day from the strip at the top
how.4: You'll see the date, time, room and teacher

subscribe.title: How to subscribe to a teacher
subscribe.body: This is the important one — without it your schedule stays empty.

how.2: Tap the subject to expand it and show its groups
how.3: Check the group's times, teacher and centre
how.4: Press “Subscribe monthly” — or pick the lesson from the list first, then “Book session”
how.5: Complete the payment, and the group appears in your schedule

payWallet.title: How to top up and pay from your wallet
payWallet.body: Top it up once and pay from it afterwards without entering card details each time.

how.3: Enter the amount in pounds, confirm and complete the payment
how.4: When subscribing to a group, choose “pay from wallet” instead of a card

payWallet.note: Wallet payments are all or nothing: if your balance is short the whole payment is refused and no part of it is taken.

subscriptions.title: How to tell whether your subscription has ended
subscriptions.body: A monthly subscription ends on its own, and nobody renews it for you. This screen shows every one you have with the date it ends.

how.2: “Running now” holds the ones still covering you, each with the days left beside it
how.3: If one says “Ending soon” or “Ended”, tap “Renew”
how.4: Renewing takes you to your subjects, where you pick the same group and pay again

subscriptions.note: When one is about to end you also get a notice on the home screen, so you do not have to go looking.

receipts.title: How to get a receipt
receipts.body: Every payment has a numbered receipt — your proof if anything goes wrong with the centre.

how.2: Tap the “Receipts” tab at the top
how.4: On the receipt page tap “Print”, or choose “Save as PDF” to send it on WhatsApp

card.title: How to get your card and use it
card.body: It carries your eight-character code — what you give the counter staff every day to be checked in.

how.1: Tap “My ID” in the bottom bar
how.2: The card opens ready — there is nothing to press
how.3: Tap “Print” to cut it out for your wallet, or “Share card” to send it on WhatsApp
how.4: At the centre: read the code to the counter, or show them the card

card.note: If the card doesn't appear, the screen tells you exactly what's missing — complete it and press “Show my card” again.

attendance.title: How to check you were marked present
attendance.body: You don't record attendance in the app — it happens at the centre, and this is where you check that it did.

how.2: At the top: present / late / absent
how.3: Below it, a coloured day map showing your consistency
how.4: If a lesson is missing, contact the centre with its date

attendance.note: If your group uses two check-ins, the counter alone is not attendance — you must also check in at the hall door.

grades.title: How to read your grades
grades.body: Every grade your teacher recorded, with your percentage and band per subject.

how.2: Find the subject in the list
how.3: Next to it: the number of entries, your score and your band

grades.note: The pass mark is 50%. If a grade is wrong, your teacher is the one who can change it.

messages.title: How to message your teacher
messages.body: If you have a question outside class, you can write to your teacher or your centre.

how.3: Pick the name from the list — it only shows people you're allowed to message
how.4: Type in the box at the bottom and send

unlockMessaging.title: If messaging is locked — how to unlock it
unlockMessaging.body: If you're under 18 with no guardian email on file, messaging teachers and centre staff is locked. It isn't a punishment — it's so a parent can see how you communicate with adults.

how.2: Find the notice asking for a guardian email
how.3: Enter your guardian's email — it must be theirs, not yours

unlockMessaging.note: A guardian phone number alone isn't enough. And everything else works normally while you're locked: your classes, grades and wallet.

pushNotifications.title: How to turn on phone notifications
pushNotifications.body: So you're told the moment a grade is recorded or a payment goes through, even with Edura closed.

how.4: Your browser asks for permission — press “Allow”

pushNotifications.note: Add Edura to your phone's home screen first; notifications work better that way.

family.title: How to link your parent
family.body: Once linked, they can see your attendance and grades, and pay for you from their own money.

how.2: You'll find a code that belongs to you at the top
how.3: Give that code to your parent — to them only

family.note: If you think the code reached someone it shouldn't have, press “Rotate Code” and the old one stops working immediately.

practice.title: And if you'd rather try it first
practice.body: There's a full practice copy you can rehearse on without paying a piastre or touching your account.

how.2: It walks you through it: read your board, subscribe to a teacher, top your wallet up and pay from it, and get your ID card
how.3: All the data is invented and no money moves

finish.title: That's it — your turn 🎉
finish.body: The tour is done. If you haven't subscribed to a teacher yet, start with “Subjects”. And if you'd rather practise first on a copy with no real money involved, open “Practice” in the menu.

studentTour.moreHint: On a phone: press “More” first — it's inside there.
